opening_paragraph: The site map for myCHEF Dubai. This site map lists every page on mychef.ae, grouped by type, so you can reach any service, location, cuisine, guide or article in one click.

A site map is a single page that lists every URL on a website in one place, so a reader or a crawler can reach any page without guessing at the navigation. This one covers every published route in 9 groups.

The groups run in the order the site is built: 12 main services, 104 occasion, format and cuisine pages, 15 Dubai locations, 15 guides, 20 blog articles, 4 chef profiles, 4 partner pages, 27 company pages and 4 legal pages.

If you know the occasion, go to the occasion page — wedding, birthday, corporate, yacht, villa — because each one carries its own price anchor and lead time. If you know the cuisine, the cuisine pages list what each kitchen covers and any dietary variants. If you are still comparing, start in the guides section, which is built to be worked through in decision order instead of browsed.

For pricing, two pages do the work: the prices page carries the per-person rates and packages, and the catering prices guide explains how a quote is assembled so you can read anyone's proposal. Rates run in two bands. Volume formats such as a working lunch, an event buffet or a premium buffet start from AED 90, AED 120 and AED 150 per person. A private chef cooking and serving on site is AED 700 to AED 950 per person. Volume formats carry a 10-guest minimum, 20 for a buffet, and a AED 900 minimum order. Every UAE catering quote carries 5% VAT on top.

new_paragraphs: The site is built in four layers. Hubs cover the broad service — private chef, catering, events, corporate, yachts, villas. Service pages sit under them for specific formats such as grazing tables, live stations, bar service and meal prep. Location pages cover 15 Dubai communities and the access and kitchen detail that changes between them. Guides and blog hold the planning reading.

Every page links upward to its hub and outward to its near neighbours, so you can move between a format, an occasion and an area without returning to the homepage. Booking runs through one route throughout: send your date, guest count and venue, and an itemised proposal follows.

add_block.new_heading: What sits behind the page names
new_paragraphs: Three page families do most of the work, and knowing which one you want saves a lot of clicking. A format page (buffet, grazing table, canapés, live stations, drop-off) describes the food and how it reaches the table. An occasion page (wedding, birthday, baby shower, corporate dinner) describes the run of the evening and the numbers that usually come with it. A location page covers access, parking, lift and kitchen detail for one Dubai community, because those change more between areas than the menu does.

Where two pages seem to overlap, the format page carries the price and the occasion page carries the planning. A wedding buffet, for example, is priced on the buffet page and planned on the wedding page.
